A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Cognac research. All 21 pages of v1 and 26 pages of v3, including appendices, are readable and support comparison across renamed datasets, relocated analyses, and revised displays.

before.justification: v1 reports original graph-unlearning experiments, baseline comparisons, GAT evaluations, and ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and adds results on further datasets, trigger poisoning, component behavior, and neighbor-selection strategies.

M1.justification: Feature inversion and top-k affected-node identification, the sigmoid contrastive loss, and alternating ascent/descent with separate optimizers remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 moves to Appendix C. The added theoretical development and MEGU-sampling ablation do not establish a change to the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Coverage expands from six to ten datasets, adding standard Cora, CiteSeer, PubMed, and OGB-Arxiv. v1's Cora is CoraFull, and Amazon is Photos; these are retained. v3 also adds edge-attack evaluations on DBLP, Physics, and Computers, plus trigger-based feature poisoning on Photos, Cora, and CS.

E2.justification: v3 Figure 4 adds Finetune and substantially expands comparator membership on retained datasets. The DBLP, Physics, and Computers node comparisons in v1 Figure 8 contain GNNDelete, MEGU, and SCRUB; v3 additionally includes GIF, UtU, AC DC, Retrain, and Finetune. The original five principal unlearning baselines remain.

E3.justification: Reported manipulation settings change across retained datasets: CoraFull added edges increase from 0.60% to 1.20%, while CS manipulated nodes change from 2.00% to 2.25% and added edges from 2.00% to 1.83%. The trigger experiment introduces feature-index modification and target-label assignment. These reported protocol revisions prevent interpreting revised scores as same-setting gains; the general split, tuning budget, and time cutoff remain.

E4.justification: v3 adds positive/negative similarity convergence analysis, fuller component comparisons, and a Cognac-versus-MEGU neighbor-selection ablation. Conversely, v1 Section 6.3/Table 4's single-versus-decoupled optimizer experiments disappear. Large-deletion, unlinking, undertraining, and top-k sensitivity analyses are retained or relocated, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions state that results are averaged across five seeds. However, v3 Table 2 omits the plus/minus uncertainty entries shown in v1 Table 2, and the replacement GAT plot omits the explicit uncertainty values previously tabulated. Several appendix tables retain plus/minus reporting; no increase in repeated runs is established.

E6.justification: v3 replaces or expands the main accuracy curves and reports many new results, including OGB-Arxiv and trigger poisoning. For example, Table 6 reports Cognac affected accuracy of 78.2 on Cora and 93.6 on CS under trigger poisoning. GAT remaining-accuracy results and optimizer-ablation scores disappear. The large-deletion and unlinking tables retain their earlier numerical results.

T1.justification: v1 contains no corresponding theorems. v3 adds an attack-entanglement theorem, a receptive-field lemma, a contrastive-separation theorem, explicit assumptions, and Appendix A proofs. However, Appendix A.2's bounded-gradient and small-step argument does not establish the claimed nonnegative separation update.

C1.justification: The central corrective-unlearning, 5%-identification, and efficiency claims remain. v3 adds an explicit large-dataset scalability claim in the abstract and drops the earlier 'first method' formulation. Its conclusion also omits v1's qualification that nearly matching the oracle requires additional manipulation information.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations connecting sigmoid contrastive loss to optimization stability and component complementarity to label supervision. It removes the discussion explaining optimizer decoupling and near-zero ascent rates for edge attacks. Homophily and real-world applicability caveats remain, but explicit warnings about simultaneous manipulations and adaptive attacks are shortened away.

D1.justification: v3 adds project and code links, explicit training-node counts, and trigger-construction details. It removes v1's explicit Adam and linear-decay implementation description, without establishing an actual optimizer change. Hardware, five-seed averaging, 100-trial Optuna tuning, and the 25% training-time cutoff remain documented.

R1.justification: New citations support feature attacks, homophily, sigmoid contrastive learning, and poison unlearning, including Gu et al., Ma et al., Lee et al., and Delta-Influence. Some earlier references, including Defazio et al., disappear. The central positioning at the intersection of corrective and graph unlearning remains.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized: related work moves from Section 2 to Section 6, experimental setup is reordered, and the formal algorithm and unlinking discussion move into appendices. Results discussion is extensively rewritten, method explanations expand, and an appendix contents page, acknowledgements, and impact statement are added.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a two-column main layout and rebuilds the main performance figure as an 18-panel grid incorporating earlier supplemental datasets. It adds an affected-node illustration and similarity-convergence plot, revises the embedding visualization, and replaces GAT tables with a curve. Several unchanged diagnostic figures are enlarged or relocated.

improvement.justification: Broader dataset and attack coverage, stronger comparator coverage, and the sampling ablation improve empirical assessment. However, v3 removes optimizer-decoupling evidence and some uncertainty reporting, while introducing a monotonicity guarantee whose Appendix A.2 proof does not establish the required gradient-sign condition. These substantive gains and losses in evidential reliability leave the net quality direction uncertain.
